model.name: claude-opus-5[1m]
model.model_note: Both the model name and the evaluator model record this evaluating session's actual runtime identity, Opus 5 (1M context), exact model id claude-opus-5[1m], per #1058. The agent definition pins a different evaluator; the pin selects the evaluator and this record states which model actually ran. Scores are comparable only to other scores produced by claude-opus-5[1m].

element_8_sub_element_4.instruction_source: quoted verbatim in the launching message (#1059, #1077)
element_8_sub_element_4.difference: The threshold in this evaluator's own agent definition lists `external_resources` pointing at a code repository as qualifying evidence without further qualification. The quoted text adds a requirement the agent definition does not contain: 'The pointer must identify the software, not its publisher: an organisation or account root (github.com/<org>), a project homepage, or prose saying the code was released via GitHub names where to start looking and does not say what produced the release, so it scores 0. A repository, a package, an archived release or a software DOI scores 1.' The quoted text is strictly narrower.
element_8_sub_element_4.applied: The quoted text was applied as written. Under this record's evidence the distinction is decisive: the only code-hosting pointer in `external_resources` is the account root https://github.com/AI-READI, which the quoted text names explicitly as a 0. Under the evaluator's own looser definition this sub-element would have scored 1, so the tightening changes the outcome by one point on this file.

issues_detected.description: Preprocessing is described as format conversion to DICOM, Open mHealth and OMOP and as 'a combination of automated and custom processing', but no slot names the software that performed it. There is no `software_and_tools`, no `machine_annotation_tools`, and the preprocessing entries carry only prose. The only code-hosting pointer is the account root github.com/AI-READI, which identifies the publisher of the code rather than the code.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add `software_and_tools` naming the conversion and curation pipelines (for example the named AI-READI repositories that perform the .fda/.sdt to DICOM and .FIT to Open mHealth conversions) with versions and per-repository URLs, or point `external_resources` at the specific repositories and their archived releases rather than the organisation root.

issues_detected.description: `third_party_sharing.is_shared` is true and five distribution formats are declared, but there is no `download_url` slot. The access route is documented only inside `data_governance.access_review_process` (https://fairhub.io/datasets/3/access) and by the `page` landing URL.
issues_detected.recommendation: Populate `download_url` with the FAIRhub access endpoint so retrieval is discoverable from the distribution block rather than only from the governance block.

issues_detected.description: `regulatory_restrictions.confidentiality_level` is set to `restricted` while the record's own note states that the only confidentiality level any source gives is the RO-Crate's HL7:2N (normal), and that the substituted value 'does not reproduce, and on its face contradicts' the source term. The substitution is disclosed and reasoned from the access gate, but the recorded value is not the sourced one.
issues_detected.recommendation: Retain the disclosure and, if the enum permits, carry the HL7 term verbatim in a notes-adjacent slot or propose an enum value that maps HL7 confidentiality codes, so the coded value and the source value do not diverge silently.

issues_detected.description: `sensitive_elements.sensitive_elements_present` is true (RO-Crate enumeration of EHR, wearable, ECG, environmental and CGM categories) while `confidential_elements.confidential_elements_present` is false and the FAIRhub healthsheet answers that the public release contains no sensitive data. The record records both positions and states that the source ranking cannot decide between them.
issues_detected.recommendation: No change required for scoring; the tension is sourced and disclosed. A downstream reader should treat the sensitivity claim as source-dependent.

issues_detected.description: Deidentification is characterised three ways across sources: FAIRhub records NoDeIdentification (no identifiers collected), the RO-Crate records deidentified true, and the Nature Metabolism comment describes HIPAA Safe Harbor stripping. The record reports all three and adds that the IRB protocol shows direct identifiers were collected in the study and code-linked, none of which appear in the release.
issues_detected.recommendation: No change required. The three characterisations are reconciled by the distinction between the study's own identifier handling and the released artifact; stating that distinction explicitly in `method` would remove the apparent contradiction.

issues_detected.description: `sampling_strategies.is_sample` is false while `strategies` describes non-probability, wave-based stratified recruitment from an EHR-derived study base. The record flags the tension itself and scopes is_sample to enrollment completeness.
issues_detected.recommendation: No change required; the scoping statement is explicit. Consider a boolean whose semantics separate 'all enrolled participants included' from 'the enrolled cohort is a sample of a population'.

issues_detected.description: `ethical_reviews` documents the reviewing IRB, protocol number, approval date, reliance agreements and four named ethics reviewers, but no conflict-of-interest statement is recorded anywhere in the record.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add a conflicts-of-interest statement to `ethical_reviews`, or record explicitly that the sources declare none, so the absence is a documented answer rather than a gap.

issues_detected.description: The license name is recorded from the license document's own title ('AI-READI Data License Agreement (Version 2.0)') while the FAIRhub dataset page labels it 'Health Data License' and the FAIRhub structured metadata 'AI-READI custom license v2.0'. Three names for one instrument, disclosed in the caveat.
issues_detected.recommendation: No change required; the document title is the defensible choice and the alternatives are recorded.

semantic_insights: The DOI prefix 10.60775 is FAIRhub's DataCite prefix and is used consistently across `id`, `doi`, `citation` and `version_access.latest_version_doi`, and the two predecessor versions carry the sibling DOIs 10.60775/fairhub.1 and .2.

Internal arithmetic reconciles exactly: the nine data-type file collections sum to 356,334 files and, with the nine root metadata files, to the declared total of 356,343. The record states that the root count is its own subtraction rather than a reported figure.

Participant arithmetic reconciles across four independent breakdowns: the three recommended splits sum to 2,280, and the race/ethnicity (380+545+519+836), sex (951+1,329) and diabetes-status (776+560+686+258) distributions each sum to 2,280.

Grant numbers follow NIH patterns for their stated mechanisms: OT2OD032644 (Other Transaction, Office of the Director, the Bridge2AI award), P30DK035816 (NIDDK center grant) and UL1TR003096 (NCATS CTSA).

Standards conformance is expressed twice, once as prose in `conforms_to` and once as a controlled list in `conforms_to_standard`, and the two agree item for item across CDS, RO-Crate, DICOM, OMOP CDM, WFDB, Open mHealth and ESDS; each file collection repeats the standard applicable to it.

Twenty collection mechanisms are documented at instrument level with manufacturer, model, city and acquisition protocol, which is materially beyond the sub-element's requirement and supports replication.

The record repeatedly separates the study from the released artifact: banked biospecimens, the controlled-access companion and the raw device exports are each named and excluded from scope, and `description` states the exclusion in its closing sentence.

Source disagreements are handled by an explicit ranking rule rather than by silent selection: eight `source_caveats` blocks record the losing position alongside the recorded one, including the acronym expansion, the lead institution, the publisher and the collection start date.

Bias documentation uses the schema's bias-type enumeration across four categories (selection, representation, sampling, measurement) with a mitigation strategy on three of them, rather than free prose.

Deidentification is semantically appropriate to the data type: identity is protected by withholding sex, race, ethnicity, medications and ZIP code to a controlled release rather than by perturbing the imaging and physiological signals, which perturbation would destroy.

sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Human subjects condition met on external fields: `description` (E1) states '2,280 adults with and without type 2 diabetes mellitus' and 'a single in-person study visit'; `collection_mechanisms` (E8) describes REDCap e-consent recruitment and participant testing. The governance disjunct is also satisfied by `regulatory_restrictions` (E2), which states constraints that apply.
sub_elements.evidence: human_subject_research.irb_approval: 'University of Washington Institutional Review Board protocol STUDY00016228. Initial approval was received on 20 December 2022, with reliance agreements covering ... the University of Alabama at Birmingham and the University of California, San Diego'; ethical_reviews with the reviewing organisation and four named ethics reviewers; data_protection_impacts recording that no DPIA was conducted

elements.name: Technical Transparency (Data Collection and Processing)
elements.description: Can data collection and processing steps be replicated or understood?

sub_elements.name: Collection Mechanisms and Settings Described
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Data collection identified (`acquisition_methods` and `collection_mechanisms` populated) and the datasets shared condition met (distribution_formats, resolvable access endpoint, third_party_sharing.is_shared true).
sub_elements.evidence: collection_mechanisms: twenty entries, e.g. 'Heidelberg Spectralis HRA+OCT (Heidelberg Engineering, Heidelberg, Germany) ... protocols are optic nerve head radial circle high resolution, posterior pole macula 61-line high resolution, and 20x20 macular OCTA'; collection_timeframes 2023-07-19 to 2025-05-01

sub_elements.name: Data Acquisition Methods Listed
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same condition as sub-element 1.
sub_elements.evidence: acquisition_methods: was_directly_observed true for laboratory, vital-sign, vision, imaging, ECG, monofilament, CGM, wearable and environmental data; was_reported_by_subjects with was_validated_verified true for REDCap questionnaire responses, verified by cross-referencing medications physically brought in; raw_sources describing the retained device and REDCap exports
sub_elements.quality_note: Both named fields populated, with the observation/self-report split flagged structurally and a concrete verification procedure.

sub_elements.name: Preprocessing, Cleaning, Labeling, and Annotation Quality
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Borderline condition resolved to applicable under the ambiguity rule: `external_resources` (E10) carries a code-hosting pointer, https://github.com/AI-READI, and `purposes` (E7) identifies the production of standards including the Clinical Dataset Structure as a project output. Neither is unambiguous, so the default is applicable and scored.
sub_elements.evidence: preprocessing_strategies: mapping to OMOP CDM, DICOM, WFDB and Open mHealth; conversion of .fda and .sdt exports to DICOM and .FIT exports to Open mHealth; cleaning_strategies: REDCap range flagging, skip-pattern checks, duplicate detection, editing only under site PI approval, and a site data manager responsible for QC before upload; instances.label false with label_description explaining that no labeling was performed because the dataset is hypothesis-agnostic; missing_data_documentation.handling_strategy stating no imputation
sub_elements.quality_note: Preprocessing, cleaning, labeling and imputation are each answered substantively, including two explicit negatives (no labeling, no imputation) with reasons.

sub_elements.name: Software and Tools Documented
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Same borderline condition as sub-element 3, resolved to applicable under the ambiguity rule.
sub_elements.evidence: No `software_and_tools` slot; no `machine_annotation_tools`; `preprocessing_strategies` entries carry only `preprocessing_details` prose naming target formats ('converted to DICOM', 'converted to the mHealth standard', 'a combination of automated and custom processing') and no tool; the only code-hosting pointer in `external_resources` is 'GitHub organization of the AI-READI project, https://github.com/AI-READI'
sub_elements.quality_note: No tooling slot carries the evidence, which is what takes the point. Applying the quoted threshold verbatim: github.com/AI-READI is an organisation root that identifies the publisher of the code, not the software that produced the release, so it scores 0; the Zenodo community root is likewise a container rather than an archived release. The software named elsewhere is incidental to slots about other things - REDCap and the MoCA Duo application inside collection mechanisms, the OMOP Data Quality Dashboard file inside a file-collection description, FAIRhub and Microsoft Azure inside the maintainer entry - which the threshold scores 0. A reader cannot tell from this record what software produced version 3.0.0.

sub_elements.name: External Standards and Resources Referenced
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met.
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: BMJ Open protocol (10.1136/bmjopen-2024-097449), Nature Metabolism comment (10.1038/s42255-024-01165-x), CDS specification v0.1.1 at cds-specification.readthedocs.io, docs.aireadi.org; conforms_to naming seven standards

sub_elements.name: Known Limitations Documented
sub_elements.evidence: known_limitations: six typed entries covering representativeness, coverage (English-language eligibility), temporal (cross-sectional, single visit), scope (withheld variables and biospecimens), methodological (no labels) and integration (Snellen variables dropped)
sub_elements.quality_note: Each entry carries a limitation_type and most carry a scope_impact or recommended_mitigation, so the consequence for a reuser is stated rather than left implicit.

sub_elements.name: Biases Categorized Using Standard Taxonomy (RAI-aligned)
sub_elements.evidence: known_biases: selection_bias, representation_bias, sampling_bias and measurement_bias, three with mitigation_strategy and one with affected_subsets; future_use_impacts: two entries including the auditability consequence of withholding sex and race
sub_elements.quality_note: Uses the schema's bias-type enumeration rather than free prose, and the measurement-bias entry identifies a real confound between device model and site.

sub_elements.name: Data Anomalies and Quality Issues Noted
sub_elements.evidence: anomalies: survey skips and incomplete responses; wearable battery failure with the Garmin two-to-three-day recharge interval; imaging noise, operator dependence and FLIO's one-centimetre motion tolerance
sub_elements.quality_note: Device- and modality-specific rather than generic, and consistent with the missing-data causes recorded separately.

sub_elements.name: Sensitive Content and Warnings Provided
sub_elements.evidence: sensitive_elements: sensitive_elements_present true, enumerating EHR, wearable monitoring, ECG, environmental sensor, CGM and accelerometer categories; confidential_elements: present false with the HL7:2N confidentiality level; the source_caveat recording that the healthsheet takes the opposite position
sub_elements.quality_note: Both slots answered, and the disagreement between the RO-Crate and the healthsheet is carried openly rather than resolved by picking the convenient side.

sub_elements.name: Ethical Review Details Including Conflicts
sub_elements.evidence: ethical_reviews: 'University of Washington Institutional Review Board ... Protocol STUDY00016228, initially approved 20 December 2022, with the initial approval letter published alongside the dataset documentation'; reliance agreements; the four named ethics reviewers Camille Nebeker, Debra Mathews, Kadija Ferryman and Nicholas Evans
sub_elements.quality_note: Reviewing organisation, protocol, date, reliance structure, published approval letter and named reviewers. No conflict-of-interest statement appears anywhere in the record, which is logged as a low-severity gap; the review documentation itself is complete and specific.

elements.name: Cross-Platform and Community Integration
elements.description: Does the dataset connect to wider data ecosystems, repositories, or standards?

sub_elements.name: Dataset Published on a Recognized Platform
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met (distribution_formats, resolvable page and access endpoint, third_party_sharing.is_shared true).
sub_elements.evidence: publisher: https://fairhub.io/; page: https://fairhub.io/datasets/3; maintainers describing FAIRhub as an Azure-hosted curation and sharing platform built for the project; external_resources naming the Zenodo community
sub_elements.quality_note: FAIRhub is a recognised health-data repository and the DOI prefix corroborates it. The record notes that the RO-Crate names the AI-READI Consortium as publisher instead, and states which source it followed.

sub_elements.name: Citation and DOI for Cross-referencing
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Publication identified in `external_resources` (BMJ Open 2025;15:e097449 and Nature Metabolism 6:2210-2212, both with DOIs) and the datasets shared condition met.
sub_elements.evidence: citation: 'AI-READI Consortium. (2025). Flagship Dataset of Type 2 Diabetes from the AI-READI Project (3.0.0) [Data set]. FAIRhub. https://doi.org/10.60775/fairhub.3'; doi: 10.60775/fairhub.3
sub_elements.quality_note: A complete DataCite-style citation with creator, year, title, version, repository and resolvable DOI.

sub_elements.name: Community Standards or Schema Conformance
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met.
sub_elements.evidence: conforms_to_standard: [CDS, RO_CRATE, DICOM, OMOP_CDM, WFDB, OPEN_MHEALTH, ESDS]; conforms_to prose binding each standard to the data it governs; per-collection conforms_to on all ten file collections
sub_elements.quality_note: Seven community standards declared at dataset level and repeated at collection level, including OMOP and DICOM which the rubric names explicitly.

sub_elements.name: Outreach Materials and Documentation Links
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met.
sub_elements.evidence: external_resources: docs.aireadi.org with a note that the dataset relies on it for provenance, data domains, variables, formats and example outputs; aireadi.org with team and contact pages; the CDS specification; page and access URLs
sub_elements.quality_note: A documentation site pinned to this version, a project site with contact routes, and the documentation's own CC-BY 4.0 licence stated.

sub_elements.name: Related Datasets with Typed Relationships
sub_elements.applicability_evidence: Datasets shared condition met.
sub_elements.evidence: related_datasets: is_new_version_of 10.60775/fairhub.2, is_new_version_of 10.60775/fairhub.1, is_source_of the AI-READI mini-subset, is_supplemented_by the controlled-access release
sub_elements.quality_note: Four relationships, three distinct types, two with resolvable DOI targets; for the two without identifiers the record states that none exist in the declared sources rather than inventing one.

strengths: Source disagreements are carried rather than resolved silently: eight source_caveats blocks record the losing position alongside the recorded one, covering the acronym expansion, lead institution, publisher, licence name, collection start date, deidentification characterisation, sampling claim and sensitivity claim.

Internal arithmetic reconciles exactly on three independent axes: the ten file collections sum to the declared 356,343 files, the three recommended splits sum to 2,280 participants, and the race, sex and diabetes-status distributions each sum to 2,280.

Ethics documentation is complete across all five sub-elements, with IRB protocol STUDY00016228, its approval date and reliance structure, a named ethics review panel, a published consent form, withdrawal terms, per-category vulnerable-population answers and a $200 stipend traced to the funding award.

Collection is documented at instrument level across twenty mechanisms with manufacturer, model, city and acquisition protocol, which is enough for a reader to reason about device-model confounding, and the measurement-bias entry names that confound explicitly.

Explicit negatives are recorded as answers rather than left as gaps: no labels, no imputation, no DPIA, no external extension mechanism, no retention limit, and the deidentification techniques deliberately not applied.
weaknesses: No slot documents the software that produced the release. Preprocessing is described as automated plus custom processing with format conversions, but no tool, version or repository is named, and the only code pointer is the organisation root github.com/AI-READI.
No `download_url` slot; retrieval is discoverable only through the landing page and an access URL buried in the governance block.

The recorded `confidentiality_level` of `restricted` contradicts the only sourced value (HL7:2N, normal) by the record's own admission, so a machine reading the coded field gets a different answer from the source.
No conflict-of-interest statement accompanies the otherwise complete ethical review documentation.

Two related datasets, the mini-subset and the controlled-access companion, are named only in prose because no identifier exists in the sources, which limits automated cross-referencing to those releases.
recommendations: Add a `software_and_tools` block naming the specific AI-READI repositories, packages or archived releases that perform the .fda and .sdt to DICOM conversion, the .FIT to Open mHealth conversion and the OMOP mapping, with versions and per-repository URLs rather than the organisation root.
Populate `download_url` with the FAIRhub access endpoint so retrieval is reachable from the distribution block.

Carry the source's HL7 confidentiality term verbatim alongside the substituted enum value, or propose an enum extension that maps HL7 confidentiality codes, so the coded and sourced values cannot diverge.
Record a conflict-of-interest statement in `ethical_reviews`, or state explicitly that the sources declare none.
Watch for identifiers for the mini-subset and the controlled-access companion in future releases and convert the two prose targets in `related_datasets` to resolvable identifiers when they appear.
